wechat_qr_hint_mobile: Scan the QR with WeChat. On this phone, screenshot it, then open WeChat → Scan → pick it from your album.
data_delta_subtitle: Entries that arrived since you last opened this page. A correction counts with the entry it corrects, not as a new one.
medications_delete_confirm: Remove this plan from the active list? Its course history stays available.
medications_action_failed: That medication change could not be completed.
indicator_no_data: No indicator data yet. Upload a report or connect a source to get started.
indicator_unavailable: This deployment does not expose the health-indicator API.
indicator_no_match_hint: Try the abbreviation or the full name — both work, in any language.
compare_hint: Pick a second model to compare answers side by side.
sources_empty_body: This deployment has no device providers configured. Add provider credentials on the server to connect Garmin, Oura, Whoop and others; until then, upload files to get data in.
file_view_unavailable: File preview is not available for this file.
file_view_unauthorized: Sign in again to open this file.
mcp_url_hint: Paste into an MCP client on this computer: Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Gemini CLI take the link as it is, and Claude Desktop through the mcp-remote bridge (the README has each setup). ChatGPT and claude.ai connect from the cloud, so they need an HTTPS address they can reach. The link is your personal credential — keep it secret.
mcp_link_regenerate_confirm: The current link stops working at once. Make a new one?
mcp_link_revoke_confirm: Anything using this link loses access at once. Revoke it?
mcp_link_shown_once: Copy it now: this link is shown only once.
mcp_link_holders: Who holds a link to your record
mcp_link_holders_none: Nobody else holds a link to your record.
mcp_link_error: Could not change the link. Try again.
error_register_failed: Could not create that account. It may already exist — try signing in.
report_date_ask: No report date was found in this file, so its readings are filed under the upload day {{date}}. Which date should they carry?
report_date_current: Readings from this file are filed under {{date}}.
report_date_moved_skipped: {{n}} readings moved to {{date}}; {{skipped}} already had a reading that day and stayed
report_date_bar_one: “{{name}}” shows no report date, so its readings are filed under the upload day {{date}}.
report_date_bar_many: {{n}} of the {{total}} files you just uploaded show no report date; their readings are filed under the upload day {{date}}.
report_date_bar_sibling: Another file from the same upload is dated {{date}}.
upload_error_connection: Could not reach the server. Upload the file again.
chart_not_drawn: This chart could not be drawn.
profile_page_sub: Your own basic details — used when answering questions about your data.
profile_readonly_note: These come from your account record and are read-only here. Fields shown as “Not set” have no value on the server yet.
profile_settings_desc: Language, timezone, security and MCP access
cc_page_sub: You, and the people whose records you can reach.
cc_empty_sub: Add a family member or someone you care for, and their records become available to ask about alongside your own.
tour_welcome_desc: A quick pass over the sidebar, so you know where everything is. You can leave at any time.
tour_data_desc: Start here: upload your reports and connect your devices to bring your data in. The readings in them show up under Indicators.
tour_chat_desc: Ask questions in plain language about the data on the left. Past conversations stay in this column while you are here.
tour_profile_desc: Your own record — name, basic information, and the way into settings.
tour_care_circle_desc: The people whose records you can reach. Add a family member here, then switch to them on the Data page or when asking a question.
tour_account_desc: Settings, this walkthrough again, and signing out. That is everything — you are set.
profile_save_failed: Could not save. Please try again.
profile_basics_note: Age is calculated from your date of birth. These details are used when answering questions about your health data.
tour_indicators_desc: Your readings, standardized into one set of units whichever source they came from. Once you have data, this is the page you land on.
drive_empty_title: Start by bringing your data in
drive_empty_body: No readings here yet. Pick any of these to start — once they are sorted, the readings show up under Indicators.
drive_empty_report_hint: Lab results or a check-up, as a PDF
drive_empty_image_hint: A picture of a lab sheet or an ultrasound report
drive_empty_journal_hint: Say what is bothering you, in a sentence
drive_empty_device_hint: Sync readings from your watch or band
journal_subtitle: Write anything, in your own words; one sentence can hold several things. Symptoms and diagnoses are matched to ICPC-3 and readings to LOINC; a medication goes onto your medication list (Indicators › Medications); anything else is kept as a note. Every entry keeps your words.
journal_placeholder_symptom: How do you feel? e.g. headache, sore throat
journal_error_too_long: Keep it under 200 characters: this is a complaint, not a diary entry.
journal_error_note_too_long: The note is longer than 2000 characters.
journal_error_failed: This entry could not be saved.
journal_not_coded_hint: No standard term matched these words.
journal_count: {{total}} entries, {{coded}} matched to a standard term
journal_empty_hint: Write how you feel above. What you log here can be read back beside your readings.
journal_load_failed: The journal could not be loaded.
journal_reason_ambiguous: Those words name more than one standard term, so none was chosen. A more specific word usually lands.
journal_reason_no_match: No standard term matched these words.
journal_reason_too_broad: That is a category rather than one complaint.
journal_placeholder_condition: What were you diagnosed with? e.g. hypertension, asthma
journal_placeholder_sentence: Anything: headache since this morning, BP 150/95, metformin 500 mg twice a day, noodles for lunch
journal_skip_negated: you said you don't have it
journal_skip_not_a_record: not a symptom, diagnosis or reading
journal_skip_not_in_sentence: not found in what you wrote
journal_skip_unclear: Not clear whether it is present or not
journal_sentence_unavailable: This server can't read a sentence yet, so log one entry at a time and pick its kind.
genomics_intro: Upload a raw consumer DNA export to make its variants available in your record. This page shows only a collection summary, never individual genotypes.
genomics_formats: WeGene, 23andMe, AncestryDNA, MyHeritage/FTDNA and VCF exports. Text, CSV, gzip/BGZF and ZIP are accepted; a VCF ZIP may include BED/TXT sidecars. The server checks the contents.
genomics_replace_note: One active genotype collection per person. A successful new upload replaces the active collection; the current one remains available until processing finishes.
genomics_replace_confirm: Upload this genotype export? If processing succeeds, it will replace this person's active genotype collection.
genomics_upload_processing: Processing genotype data… The current collection remains active.
genomics_upload_failed: The upload or processing failed. The previous collection remains active.
genomics_upload_invalid: Choose a nonempty genotype TXT, CSV, VCF, gzip or ZIP file.
genomics_pending_endpoint: Collection summary is not available on this server yet. Upload progress is still shown here.
genomics_load_error: Could not load the collection summary. Try opening this tab again.
genomics_old_set_active: This collection stays active while the replacement is processed.
records_export_failed: The export could not be downloaded.
medications_schedule_locked: This plan has more than one dosing instruction; its schedule stays as it is. Name, strength and dates can still be changed here.
journal_placeholder_note: Anything else: a meal, a mood, how you slept
journal_med_not_on_list: not on your medications, nothing to stop
journal_meds_failed: The medications in that sentence could not be saved. Try again.
medications_instructions: How to take it (e.g. after meals)
medications_empty_hint: Write it in Data › Records, e.g. “metformin 500 mg morning and evening”, and it appears here.
invite_sign_in_desc: You get a one-time link to send {{name}}. When they open it and confirm their email, the record you keep for them becomes theirs, and they choose what you can still see.
invite_sign_in_copy_failed: Could not copy. Select the link and copy it by hand.
invite_sign_in_hint_code: Send this link to {{name}} any way you like. It works once, until {{date}}. They confirm it with a code sent to {{email}}.
invite_sign_in_hint_password: Send this link to {{name}} any way you like. It works once, until {{date}}. They set a password for {{email}} (or enter it, if that address already has an account).
cc_sharing_sub: The people whose circle you are in. Change what each of them can see at any time.
activate_intro: {{creator}} has been keeping a health record for you on Mirobody ({{member}}). Activate it to sign in yourself; everything already recorded stays.
activate_password_hint: At least 8 characters. If this email already has an account, enter its password.
activate_password_optional_hint: Set one to sign in with a password as well as a code.
activate_access_edit: Keep viewing and managing my record
activate_invalid_text: It has been used, has expired, or was replaced by a newer one. Ask the person who sent it for a new link.
settings_model_desc: A model service, or 100% on this machine: where your documents and questions are processed.
setup_title_first: Choose who reads your health data
setup_intro: Mirobody uses a model to read your reports and answer your questions. Pick where that model runs.
setup_promise_record: Your record stays in this deployment's database either way
setup_promise_encrypted: Keys and addresses are stored encrypted
setup_promise_change: Change it any time in Settings
setup_mode_key_desc: Connect OpenRouter, OpenAI, Gemini, DeepSeek and others with one API key.
setup_mode_local_desc: Two open models run on this computer through llama.cpp. No key, no account.
setup_key_privacy: Questions and documents are sent to that service
setup_local_speed: Slower than a service; on a CPU alone, a first answer takes minutes
setup_local_privacy: Questions and documents never leave this machine
setup_local_needs: From 16 GB of memory, by size; Small needs no GPU
setup_key_stored: The key is stored encrypted in this deployment's database and sent only to its own service. One test request checks it before it is kept.
setup_local_open: Both are open models run by llama.cpp, which has builds for macOS, Linux and Windows.
setup_local_mac_note: Apple silicon. llama.cpp runs on the Mac itself, where it can use the GPU. Run this in the mirobody folder, where deploy.sh is.
setup_local_gpu_note: An NVIDIA GPU, on Linux (with the NVIDIA Container Toolkit) or on Windows with Docker Desktop. The models run in a container next to Mirobody. Run this in the mirobody folder.
setup_local_cpu_note: Any computer with Docker, no GPU needed. The models run on the CPU in a container next to Mirobody, so choose Small: on 4 CPU cores a first answer takes 2–3 minutes. Docker needs at least 8 GB of memory for them; Docker Desktop gives it half the computer's by default. Run this in the mirobody folder.
setup_local_other_note: Other setups: the guide has the steps.
setup_local_address_hint: Left empty, Mirobody looks at {{list}}, in that order.
setup_local_submit: Use the models on this machine
setup_local_saved: Mirobody now uses the models on this machine. The first start downloads them, and the first answer waits until they are loaded.
setup_local_all_ready: Both models are loaded. Mirobody is ready.
setup_token_hint: It is SETUP_TOKEN in the .env next to compose.yaml, and the link ./deploy.sh printed carries it.
setup_token_hint_log: Until a model is set up, the app's log prints that link too: docker compose logs mirobody | grep setup
setup_too_many: Too many wrong tokens. Wait ten minutes and try again.
setup_sign_in_needed: A model is already set up, so changing it takes a signed-in account. Sign in and you will come back here.
setup_load_failed: Could not reach the server. Reload the page to try again.
setup_key_rejected: The service did not accept this key or model name.
setup_local_not_found: No model server with these models was found.
setup_fixed_in_env: This is set in .env, which comes first.
setup_model_hint: Model names change often: type the one {{label}} lists now.
setup_model_spaces: A model name has no spaces.
setup_key_turns_on: Chat uses {{chat}}; documents are read by {{utils}}.
setup_privacy_key: With a key, your questions and documents are sent to {{label}}.
setup_privacy_local: 100% on this machine: your questions and documents are processed here, and none of it leaves this machine.
setup_checking_wait: This can take up to a minute and a half ({{seconds}} s so far).
setup_find_intro: Ask the model server whether it has the models you chose.
setup_not_served: {{models}} is not on that server. Load it there, or choose one it serves.
setup_local_windows_note: Windows 10 or 11. This is llama.cpp's Vulkan build: it uses an Intel, AMD or NVIDIA GPU, else the CPU. Run it in PowerShell, in the mirobody folder: for a clone in WSL, first cd \\wsl.localhost\Ubuntu\home\<you>\mirobody
setup_local_models_max: --models-max 2 keeps one answering model and the document reader loaded, so choosing another size unloads the one before.
setup_tier_intro: Small runs on an ordinary computer; Large answers better and needs more memory.
setup_tier_text_only: Gets their text from the reader
setup_tier_hw_light: Any computer with 16 GB of memory, no GPU needed — Windows, Linux or Mac
setup_tier_hw_large: A Mac with 32 GB, or an NVIDIA GPU with 24 GB
setup_tier_unloaded: On this server, not loaded yet
setup_pair_loaded: Both models are on this server and loaded.
setup_pair_unloaded: Both models are on this server but not loaded yet. Mirobody will ask the server to load them; the first load downloads them.
